brief: THE BET, and the first new BUILDING since the loop began: a watermill on the far bank. A mill house at the towpath's edge — a real footprint in buildGrid()/solidM so buildVolumes() grows its roof and eaveFor() gives it a height — with an undershot wheel hanging over the water column beside it, turning every frame at a rate off riverRun() (faster in the grey season), slowing to a stop as the river ices (riverCol/fountainIce are the frost's existing readers; pick the one the river already uses), with a tail-race streak in drawRiverFlow(t) and a lit window at night via FACES[]/windowLit so the far bank has a light after dark. Register it in nameAt/pavingAt's family so the sill says 'the mill'. Site: the worker chooses between the north end (rows 18–22, between the nave and the first orchard tree) and the south end (rows 56–61, past the orchard) after checking what walks there — TOW_WALK 128.6, FAR_WALK 133.2, EAST_GATE_P, DECK_LEAD_Q — and where the boat runs (boat.x), because the wheel must not sit on the boat's line. The wheel and its shadow are two draw items round anything that walks the towpath (the #73 law). A 150–300-line diff is expected and welcome. developed, structures and possibly water MUST move: re-pin the census baseline with census.mjs --save-baseline and say so in the entry.
successLooksLike: From the wide shot at noon, something on the far bank is turning — all day, every day, faster after rain, still at midwinter. At 03:00 the mill has a window lit. The census baseline moves (developed, structures) and is re-pinned deliberately.
avoid: Do not build the wheel as a cached-ground paint or a sprite on the towpath; it is live geometry sorted with the walkers. Do not add a miller agent this pass — the building is the work; a miller is the next brief if the mill lands. Do not touch the church, bandstand or footbridge routes except to route AROUND the new footprint.
